messages:
anya: heads-up — saga13b int4 rolling canary (quant drop-in) started at 09:05, seeing fragmentation on a subset of hosts, intermittent OOMs on long generations
sam: can you paste the error snippet?
anya: ```
[2025-06-18T09:05:14Z] ERROR oom: failed to allocate 1.2GB for kv_cache
stack: inferer.cpp:421 allocate_kv_cache
gpu0: free 2.3GB, used 29.7GB
``` 
leo: how many tokens / max_new_tokens? config show
anya: we're using max_new_tokens=1024, batch_size=1, windowed prefetch enabled
maria: note we defaulted to `slot_reserve=0.05` for this model — might be low for int4 memory layout
sam: try bumping slot_reserve to 0.15 and enable small microbatching (batch_size=2) — also try smaller `max_new_tokens` default for canary
ryan: what's impact on latency? even small batch could add 20-30ms
anya: observed ~15ms p95 for single-token streams, but OOMs are causing tail spikes and fallback to cpu-runner
ops-bot: deploy 1756789001-canary-saga13b-quant v1 -> hosts: gpu-prod-31,gpu-prod-33
leo: can we repro locally with `prefetch=0`? maybe prefetch interacts with quantized layout and causes fragmentation
anya: on repro, disabling prefetch avoids OOM but increases cpu fallback frequency and increases token cost
sam: plan:
1) roll back prefetch in canary
2) increase slot_reserve to 0.15
3) reduce max_new_tokens default to 512 for this model
4) run 12h smoke with long-gen prompts + collect kv metrics
maria: also collect per-layer kernel mem footprint + kv hit/miss and eviction counts
anya: i'll open a canary patch, link: https://phabricator.redwood/s/PR1234 :thumbsup:
sam: assign to @leo to monitor, i'll schedule evals
leo: ack, will monitor p95 and OOM logs, will post updates
anya: thanks — keep it tight, want to avoid rollback in prod
